Welcome, Astroneers! As promised, we've got a new Major Update building on the big changes we started to introduce to the game in the Voidbreak Update back in September. We've added a new co-op Offensive that features a BIG LASER, as well as the ability to use Voice Chat with your Squad!
Add to that a spooky log-in reward for October, a new fashion contest, changes to get rid of Gear breaking, and bringing back past community events, so there is plenty to cover. Let’s get into it.

If you just joined us, we want to make sure you understand how much of the game has changed since the early access launch in June. There are several new Landing Sites granting access to explore most Regions of the planet Tephra, dozens of new pieces of Gear, and new features like matchmaking for Squads. Today’s update also completes our first wave of Voidbreak Offensives, a new type of Expedition introduced in our previous update built to offer some challenge and structured gameplay!

We know that the game at launch didn’t land with players the way we wanted, and we have made big strides to push towards a new direction. Thank you so much to all of the players who have jumped in and given us thoughtful and honest feedback.

That being said, the Laser Array Update builds off the foundations laid by the Voidbreak Update, like deprecating the Gear breaking feature and adding Voice Chat, a HIGHLY requested feature. We hope these changes will encourage players to collaborate more and maybe take some extra risks. Matchmake into Squads and make some friends! (Or don’t, voice chat is completely optional) On top of that, we've also added another Voidbreak Offensive: Laser Array!

I wanted to address this right up front here. Voidbreak Offensives aren't meant to be the sole focus of the game. We would like to think that they add to the experience, giving players some repeatable and interesting things to do in between Free Roam Expeditions down to the planet. We're still working on big changes coming to Free Roam that we think you'll be excited about and will go a long way toward making all of these pieces fit together. Expect to see another big update before the end of the year. We're also going to continue iterating on Voidbreak Offensives based on your feedback.

A Void Mass has been spotted in the Sinking Reef. Readings show a cavernous interior, but attempts to access the core have failed. Build a massive laser to blast your way inside.

That Void Mass of pure corruption must be destroyed! If left unchecked, the Void will quickly spread in this Region. It’s up to you and your Squad to deploy to Tephra, assemble the BFL (Bilateral Fusion Laser), and fire it directly into the source of the corruption. Defend the support sections of the construction project from aggressive creatures and then search for Useful Parts scattered nearby to finish building the Laser Array with.

Remember to use your scanner to find the outlines of Useful Parts underground. Searching around the perimeter of the Laser Array and the area nearest the Void Mass should be the most fruitful for your search. There might even be some good stuff worth salvaging inside that Void Mass. Pretty simple, right?! What could possibly go wrong?
There are some fun new mechanics in this Offensive, so make sure to share your feedback with us about how they are feeling!!!

Some of the earliest feedback we got for the game was suggesting that we add Voice Chat for players to be able to communicate in-game without the need for third-party apps. We agree wholeheartedly that co-op games like ours shine the most when communication with your squadmates can happen seamlessly, so we're excited to finally bring this feature to the game with this update!

This should match what you expect of your average Voice Chat in other games. It's not proximity based; you only hear players you invite to your Squad. You can freely adjust the input device, volume, and push-to-talk settings.

It's been tricky to add this to the game. We needed to do our research to ensure we did it right. We still know there are plenty of players out there who prefer to avoid voice comms in games or have concerns about what they might run into with voice chat on. These are legitimate concerns, so here's how we're tackling them.

For starters, Voice Chat is completely optional and will always be something you can freely choose to enable or disable. Disabling Voice Chat means you don't use it, and you don't hear other players who do use it.

If you do enable Voice Chat, you now have the option to use the Comms Wheel (used for Pings and Emotes) to quickly mute all other players. You can also go to the Social tab in the DAD menu to manually mute a specific player. Just like it is with blocked players, muted players will be kept track of in the Social menu.

Our first and top concern with adding Voice Chat to the game was ensuring that we'd be able to keep our players safe. We've done our due diligence in implementing industry standard best practices to help with moderation and identifying bad actors in Voice Chat. That said, using the in-game reporting tools will always be the strongest option in your tool set. We'll keep a close eye on your feedback following this release.

Voice Chat only comes into use with other Astroneers in your Squad, so we've sent you all a new free Emote via your Inbox to help with this (added by default for new players). The Emote is called "Join my Squad?" and lets you hold out a sign to let those around you know that you're looking for squadmates.
There's also the new Speak Easy Set of Emotes available in the EXO Outlet, grouping up some new and old Emotes that are most useful for communicating with your Squad.

That's right! As of this update, your Gear doesn't break anymore! Your Backpack slots won't get damaged either. Now, whatever Nozzles, Mods, or equippable Gear you craft will stick around no matter how badly you get knocked around. However, you can still lose any resources or consumables in your inventory if you fail an Expedition. You can also still drop Gear and lose it if you leave it behind, though it's hard to do that by accident.

In its first iteration, Gear breaking was meant to add a level of risk to your Expeditions in STARSEEKER. There should be consequences to failing, so having Gear break made sense at the time and also played into the game economy as something to channel the resources you gather into repairing your Gear.

With the game's current direction, this no longer makes sense, as it can keep you from wanting to venture into riskier challenges like those in Voidbreak Offensives. It could also lead to unwanted consequences with players losing Gear over things beyond their control, like connection issues, despite our efforts to avoid that.

Gear no longer breaking has knock-on effects on the game economy. We teased these changes recently on a livestream and some wondered what resource gathering would be good for if you're no longer having to repair your Gear. Resources are still good for crafting consumables and Gadgets, but we're also making adjustments.

Gear crafting recipes now require more resources across the board. With these changes, crafting Gear has become a long-term investment, so it's more of a milestone. For existing players, you have nothing to worry about; you'll keep the Gear you've already crafted. Your broken Gear items aren't going anywhere either, and you still have the option to repair them until our next update.

And this isn't the end to the economy changes we're working on. Once we add the updates to Free Roam that we've been talking about, there will be further adjustments that will make all recent changes to the game better fit together. More info on that soon!

We've been asked before whether past Community Challenges would be returning to the game, and as we prepare to invite new Astroneers aboard the station, it's a great time to do just that! In the coming weeks, we'll be bringing back the State of Flux and Pulp Friction Community Challenges!

These are the same Community Challenges as you remember them, though any bugs that we identified previously will have been ironed out. It's a good way for any newer players who missed out to get to experience these events, and we have a couple of additions for those of you looking to replay these challenges.
In addition to being another opportunity to earn the original cosmetic rewards for these challenges, we've added two new cosmetic rewards to each Community Challenge!

We're also experimenting with asking for more personal contributions in order to unlock these rewards. Nothing crazy, though, just enough to help incentivize more participation. These changes might inform how we set up future Community Challenges. The old rewards are all locked behind only personal contributions, while the new rewards require personal contributions and community-wide milestones.

Both the State of Flux and Pulp Friction Community Challenges have their own associated Mission chains. If you've completed these Missions before, then you won't have to do them again. Your progress is being carried over. You'll also notice that the Flux Drive will be reset during the reprised State of Flux event.

Adding Voice Chat, the Laser Array Voidbreak Offensive, its many new features, and the Identity Crisis Community Challenge represents the bulk of the work that went into this update. We still have more work to do in our next update to tackle improvements to matchmaking, fine tune Voidbreak Offensives, and overhaul the game economy, just to name a few priorities, so plenty more to come!
That said, this update also has a lot of bug fixes and other improvements worth calling out. Here are the highlights:
Reduced movement penalties for jumping, swimming, and gliding while carrying heavy items.
Increased mid-air control to help with making adjustments during jumping and platforming obstacles. Mid-air control is also possible now when letting go of a wall you’ve been climbing or clinging to.

Added a new subtab under "Objectives" in the DAD menu that shows a list of your tracked objectives. From this menu, you can choose to individually untrack any item. This provides the convenience of managing what is currently being tracked without needing to remember and go to all the different places where an objective can be tracked (i.e. Missions, Stickerbook, Data Logs, Printer, Events).

Added DLSS frame generation as an option for PCs with compatible GPUs (RTX40xx and newer) to enable frame interpolation. This helps with smoothening frames but also increases input latency. This option can be enabled and disabled in the Visuals tab of the Settings options.

Let's talk about what is on the horizon for STARSEEKER. Full transparency: STARSEEKER needs more players, and everything we have been doing has been an attempt to bring in new folks. At launch, we had a strong number of people who tried the game, but we just didn’t have enough content to keep people playing.

Now, after four back-to-back content updates and a big re-arranging of plans to the roadmap, we are feeling much better about putting the game out there. Expect to see some deeper discounts and deals across all platforms while we really try to find some players who are down with the new content and ideas we are exploring.

Our next update will go live sometime before the end of the year and will include the aforementioned changes to Free Roam and the overall economy. Expect to see more changes with lasting impact on how your Expeditions shape the Starseeker’s presence on Tephra, more variety of Nozzle rewards to chase and slot into your Gear loadout, and plenty more bits and pieces we’re eager to share.

There’s some cool stuff coming. I am super thankful to all of you who have stuck by us and shared feedback during this phase while we explored these big changes and worked to make STARSEEKER better. Watching something you worked on for years not meet expectations is very hard, but ultimately, we just want to make games that make people happy and we hope you all can see that. Talk soon.

The Voidbreak Update is a Major Update for STARSEEKER. We’re addressing feedback about the game and making significant changes to its core design to better keep you engaged in what you’re doing, more easily find other players to play with, and get a better sense of the impact your efforts are making in this world.

Big changes like these can’t be done easily in one fell swoop, so consider this update as a first step toward this new vision for the game, with much more to follow in the coming months. With this new vision in mind, the team has been working hard at pulling forward content we originally intended to add later in the development timeline, as well as new ideas.

We're really excited to get this content into players' hands! That said, we still need additional rounds of iteration, and we want your feedback to guide us in the right direction. notes.title: A NEW INTERGALACTIC THREAT – THE VOID

items.text: We've talked about our intent to introduce this game's antagonist much sooner than we originally intended to make it clear that Astroneers are pushing against something threatening that will push right back. That's the Void, a perilous cosmic entity that consumes all by corrupting anything it comes in contact with, especially life forms.

The Void is the final evolutionary state of LRDs, those mysterious monochromatic marbles. Once awakened, it stops at nothing to devour everything around it. Even the terrain becomes an extension of the Void, slowly spreading farther as it devastates the planet.

Tephra isn't the only planet in danger. The very existence of the universe depends on defeating the Void. The Starseeker is the first EXO crew to understand how deadly the Void is, and it's up to everyone on board to stop its spread.

Spawned by the Void, Voidlings are the first Void entities to be introduced. These little one-eyed blobs may not seem like much of a threat by themselves, but getting swarmed by a bunch of them or getting jumped by one while your attention is divided can spell the end of any Astroneer.

Void entities all aid in the spread of the Void in different ways. In the case of Voidlings, that comes as the ability to burst into Void puddles that corrupt both the terrain and any Astroneers the Void comes in contact with.

To defeat them, most Nozzles and damaging Canisters should do the trick, but SPA Water is the bane of the Void, so it will be most effective against them and the Void they spread. Those disturbing purple eyes are also sensitive to Astroneer scanners, so scanning a Voidling will make the eyes pop for a quick take down.

The spread of the Void threatens to engulf everything, including the terrain itself. Void Terrain appears to be covered in a monochrome swirl sludge, like an LRD spill. Void entities will do their best to spread Void Terrain, so you should do your best to clear it.

When you find growing tendrils of Void Terrain, use your scanner to identify their source. You should be able to find red spheres underground, LRDs and their decoy signals. These Void Terrain tendrils will continue growing and spawning Voidlings if left alone, but severing a tendril from its LRD origin will temporarily stop its spread and prevent Voidlings from spawning on the severed portion. As with Void entities, SPA Water can easily cleanse this corruption, but you can also deform the Void Terrain with your EXO Multi-Tool at the expense of slowly gaining some corruption.

To fully clear this Void Terrain, you must eliminate the LRD that is causing it. LRDs encase themselves in Undiggable Void Terrain, but these shells are ruptured by the tendrils of Void Terrain that grow from them. Follow the tendrils and track them back to their source. Destroy the LRDs with either SPA Water or terrain deformation, and you’ll also cleanse some of your own corruption.

Coming into contact with the Void can create a buildup of corruption that progressively cuts down your health. Your health bar will be reduced more and more, replaced with Void corruption that limits your maximum health in stages until there’s almost nothing left. It won't outright take you down, but it will leave you very vulnerable to incoming attacks.

You can use SPA Water to cleanse yourself and your Squad, but SPA Water can only do so much. There are five stages of corruption, and being exposed to corruption can push you into further stages. SPA Water can only cleanse the corruption buildup that would push you into the next stage. After reaching a stage of corruption, there’s no way to cleanse it, only returning to the Starseeker will restore your health to normal.

Bringing players together around shared goals is when STARSEEKER shines the most, and that’s what Voidbreak Offensives are meant to prioritize. Voidbreak Offensives are a new type of Expedition that represent a new game mode. You can launch from the station and be matched with other players into an instanced scenario in which only your Squad will be present, unlike Free Roam Expeditions, which are the traditional way of playing STARSEEKER that you’re already familiar with.

There are different Voidbreak Offensives you can choose from, each in a set location with goals to accomplish. This mode will present players with a greater challenge. It’s possible to fail Voidbreak Offensives if your whole Squad is wiped out, so you’ll have to prepare properly with some of your best gear in order to improve your chances of success, but know that failure will damage your gear and lose your unequipped inventory.

Launching into an Expedition is now done on different sections of the Starseeker bridge. You can still use the Launch Terminals at the bottom of the bridge to go on free Roam Expeditions. To launch into a Voidbreak Offensive, use the new Command Table, right where the planetary hologram next to Captain Jupiter used to be.

You also have the option to enable matchmaking for both modes now. You're not forced to match into a Squad or bring your own Squad to play Voidbreak Offensives, but the difficulty is tuned around Squads, so solo players will have a really challenging time.

And for those who may be wondering, we'll continue to support Free Roam Expeditions. They’re still a great way to gather resources, complete Tasks, and are generally a more chill way to play the game. Keep reading to learn more.

Voidbreak Offensives are meant to be a repeatable source of valuable rewards, which may see some further iteration in future updates as we add more ideas we’re working on and respond to feedback. Succeeding will reward everyone in your Squad with Credits, rarer resources like Carbon Fiber, and new Framework crafting items.

There are Mod Frameworks and Nozzle Frameworks. As their names suggest, they are used in crafting Mods and Nozzles, respectively, and are necessary components for crafting advanced gear. The newest Blueprints in the game for the most advanced Mods and Nozzles will be unlocked with these rewards, as well as new gear that we’re actively developing now.

This Voidbreak Offensive calls you into the cavernous maze of the Fungal Depths, where Shroomlings sing an eerie song amongst hazardous spores that are influenced by the Void. To what end? It’s hard to say. But it’s clear that the Void is benefiting from it, so it must be stopped.

Be wary of singing Shroomlings that make it to their places of worship; they’ve been known to cause Delirium. The whole Squad can fall to Delirium without the chance to revive, so watch each other’s backs and clear out those Shroomlings!

items.text: Expeditions can now land directly in the Fungal Depths Region! This dark and barren land may be inhospitable on the surface, but underneath there’s a sprawling cavern system of hardened terrain filled with bioluminescent fungal life. As mentioned earlier, Free Roam is how we’re now referring to the original way of playing Starseeker that you’re already familiar with. There's less pressure in Free Roam Expeditions, which are well suited for gathering resources, exploring, and hanging out with your Squad.

Speaking of Squads, this Update also introduces Matchmaking settings for Free Roam, letting you match into a Squad of other players looking to do some Free Roam exploring. Of course, you can also disable Matchmaking in this mode if you feel like heading out solo, though you might still run into other players roaming nearby.

We have some exciting plans for Free Roam that will also be bringing the Void into this mode, along with new ways in which you can contribute toward leaving a lasting mark on the world. This is part of the changes where we want to show players the impact they’re making with their Expeditions, and we hope to share more details on this soon.

Since we’re no longer introducing new Missions, you may be wondering how Blueprints are earned now. All new Blueprints in this Update are earned with the first successful completion of each Voidbreak Offensive. Here’s the list:

Climb Speed Mod V2 – Uplink
Goop Gel Mod – Uplink

Swim Speed Mod V2 – Core Retrieval

In future updates, we’ll be changing how previous Blueprints are earned so that new players have a consistent experience. As for all of you who have already unlocked plenty of Blueprints, those won’t be going anywhere, so don’t you worry. We also have plans for new content that will replace Missions, so more information on that soon.

There was a lot of work going into this update to add the new Voidbreak Offensives and Matchmaking infrastructure, as well as all the surrounding features that came with them. We’ll continue to iterate on all this as your feedback begins to come in. Even so, we still managed to tackle a lot of bugs and improve the overall quality of the release alongside this new content. AG-18778 – Changed the Lasso and Shock Lasso Nozzles behavior so that they can no longer latch on to other players.

Developer Note: This feature was being used to grief players, so we felt it was best to remove it. If you experience any griefing, remember you can report them in-game. Go to the Social tab in the DAD menu, select the profile of the offending player, and select Report Player.
Reduced the radius of the blast created by destroying a Null Field. Successfully eliminating one shouldn't feel like you’re being penalized now.
Made changes to Shock effects so that they now impart a little more Fatigue Buildup and reduced the time needed for Lassos to lock on to targets.
Developer Note: We noticed some feedback about the utility of the Shock Lasso that we hope these changes will help address.
Changed the duration of the Burning Status Condition from 5 seconds to 10 seconds. This also results in doubling the Fatigue Buildup by the end of the Status Condition.
AG-18500 – Added a Health bar for other members of your Squad that shows under their names when their Health is below 100%. This is to help give better awareness of Squad Health when using healing.

AG-18498 – Changed the Sell action when trading with Crew Members so that it now sells the whole selected stack by default. There’s now a secondary action to “Sell Some” noted in the bottom right corner of the window UI that lets you select the specific amount you want to sell.
AG-16993 – Made a change so that the button/key to open the DAD Menu is now the same one used to close it for both controllers and mouse & keyboard.
AG-18058 – Added an error message that now pops up when you try to equip a second Utility Mod of the same type.
AG-19270 – Made improvements to buffs affecting swim speed so that they now also improve swim speed while ascending and descending.

AG-12701 – Fixed an issue that would cause Carrotling Health bars to show while they were being held.
AG-19213 – Fixed an issue where the Resolution Scale setting could be reset despite still showing the selected value in the Settings menu.
AG-18310 – Fixed an issue that could cause controls to become unresponsive after cancelling a friend request when playing on the Nintendo Switch 2.
Fixed various other VFX, display, and animation issues.
AG-18808 – Fixed an issue that was causing the Refiner UI to show the same side tab options as the Printer UI.
AG-15364 – Fixed an issue that was preventing Field Mission: Elevation Readings from correctly displaying on the Mission tab in the End of Expedition screen.
AG-18835 – Fixed an issue where returning from an Expedition with no items in your inventory could show “Items Recovered” instead of “Items Lost” in the End of Expedition screen.
AG-19049 – Fixed an issue where Landing Site waypoints would disappear after rejoining an Expedition a player disconnected from.
AG-19110 – Fix an issue that would still show the Expedition countdown message while having the Planet View map up on the station.
AG-16858 – Fixed an issue where the waypoint for the Altimeter during Field Mission: Elevation Readings would sometimes disappear.
AG-18707 – Changed the notification message for unlocking multiple Community Challenge rewards at once so that it’s clearer now.

AG-16201 – Fixed an issue where the Expedition loading screen animation could momentarily show the icon of the Dropship heading in the opposite direction than intended while playing on the Nintendo Switch 2.
AG-18333 – Fixed an issue present in Russian language where the “Keyboard/Mouse Mapping” header text in the Settings Menu would overlaps with the description window.
AG-19025 – Fixed an issue that was preventing the Golden Pathos achievement from being granted for completing a Mission chain.
Developer Note: We’ve retroactively granted this achievement to everyone that should have earned it. Thank you to all who reported this issue!

AG-16727 – Fixed an issue where the pod with the Elevation Console for Field Ops: Elevation Readings sometimes wouldn’t spawn on Undiggable Terrain.
AG-18338 – Fixed an issue with Field Ops: Creature Wrangling where it could grant its rewards twice for a single completion.

Developer Note: We’ve also retroactively granted this Blueprint to everyone that should have earned it by completing the Mission.

A new limited time Field Ops activity is now available for the duration of the Astral Flux Community Challenge! Alongside other Astroneers, you’ll be able to leverage a massive drill (lovingly dubbed Drilliam by Muriel) to extract large amounts of Astral Flux, along with additional resources if you do a good job at keeping it cooled down and well defended.

After completing some of Blandrew’s Missions, he’ll direct you to use the EXO Drill Rover to help gather more Astral Flux. Once you track this Mission, you’ll have a marker during your Expedition to show you the way to the Field Ops: Drilling on a large island to the northeast of the Wetlands or northwest of the Tangle.

You don’t need Blandrew’s Mission to run this Field Ops, but the Mission marker can be good to help you navigate there the first time. Using the Air Blast Nozzle in combination with a Dash Mod can be a good way to make fast progress through the water, but you didn't hear that from me.

As the EXO Drill Rover drills its way through hard terrain, it will begin to overheat. A large canister in the rear corner has a meter to help you track this. Make sure to bring a Water Hose Nozzle, Water Canisters, or anything that can apply the Wet condition to the drill. This will keep the drill running efficiently, so you don't need to do repairs on the go.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45566901/38c75693f13ba8ef8842655db3aae463fc844f0a.jpg"]
There are various hazards on the path of the EXO Drill Rover that you’ll need to clear to ensure it keeps running. Things might differ from your previous run, stay alert!

Null Fields embedded in hard terrain can stop the drill in its tracks, so come prepared! Null Fields can be dug out with Excavation Canisters, or you can Goop up the area and throw Fire Canisters to blow them up (just be careful).
Explosive Kablooms may be growing on the path. Try grabbing or lassoing them with the Lasso Nozzle after they’re dug out to dispose of them.
Malfunctioning Demolition Devices may also bombard the area, so running ahead of the drill to break them down can be very helpful.

The drill knows where it's going but has no regard for what may be in its path, including Boghound Burrows, angry Brutoliths, or even Carrotlings with the insane idea of bringing you Kablooms. Make sure to keep the drill defended, especially when it stops to recalibrate its path; it won’t move until nearby nests are broken down. It will take multiple Astroneers to face off against these creatures, so keep that in mind before starting the Field Ops.

Once the Field Ops has ended, interact with the drill to claim heaps of Astral Flux nuggets as your reward. The further you manage to keep it cooled down, repaired, and well defended, the greater the rewards. Even if the drill breaks down and the Field Ops ends, make sure to still claim the Astral Flux you managed to mine.

Doing a good job at escorting the drill can also make it pop like a piñata with nuggets of other resources. The further you’re able to get the drill, and the more Astroneers participating, the more resources will pop out every time it survives an encounter. Just like a piñata, these are up for grabs for anyone who claims them first.

This update features approximately 300 bug fixes across all areas of the game. We tried to tackle some of the most visible issues you’ve reported as well as tidy things up in areas we knew needed another pass. If you don’t see a particular issue you were hoping would get addressed, don’t worry! Some things take more than a quick bug fix to resolve, and we’re working on other UX improvements (looking at you, Stash!) alongside new content for future updates. In the meantime, here are the highlights of this patch:

The Creatures team dedicated a chunk of time this update to addressing issues in all areas of the Creature system. Creature Spawners and habitats were a big area of focus, ensuring that Creatures spawn correctly, and their homes and nests react appropriately to interactions from Players. As a part of this, Creature behavior and their response to combat were revisited so that Creatures behave more reliably when waking/sleeping, attacking, or healing.

Player interactions with Creatures also received a pass, fixing several cases where sedation, scanning, and items like the Energy Leash, Camouflage Mod, and Spa Water would fail unexpectedly. Carrotlings won’t wake up so easily now and will also give a bit of a warning before entering their Enraged state. We even reminded Bog Hounds that they do, in fact, like to eat Life Fruit!
As this is one of the most complex systems in STARSEEKER, we will continue monitoring for major issues and improving all things Creatures.

Dropping an abundance of loose items in the station can cause performance issues for all players present in that instance. To address this, we’ve added a timer to remove these items after enough time has passed, 15 minutes for loose items, 30 minutes for deployable Gadgets like the Trampoline. Please be kind and don’t litter.

Developer Note: To clarify, trading stuff on the station is perfectly fine; the issue is dropping large numbers of items and letting them sit there. We’ll monitor to see if these times feel like they strike a good balance at addressing the issue and not becoming an inconvenience. We have a few other fun ideas on how we’d like to tackle this.
We’ve added more triggers to respawn players into the station if they manage to exit the intended station boundaries.

Developer Note: We’ll continue to tackle locations where players can sneak past the station walls to mess around in space and have a poke around. Even if you do manage to clip through, you should now get respawned.
To avoid confusion, we’ve updated the names of Ooze Balls and Ooze Bushes to Boingle Balls and Boingle Bushes.
Developer Note: The old name gave the impression that they might be a source of Goop, so hopefully that’s clearer now.
Seamelon Blorbs should spawn more often now in underwater biomes.

Hello, Astroneers! We hope you’ve been having fun with STARSEEKER over the weekend. We’ve got a new Patch with some performance and stability fixes we wanted to get quickly into the game, and also some answers to share for some recent community questions.
Over the weekend, Creative Director Adam also shared another update on behalf of the team that’s worth a read, if you haven’t seen it yet.

In our previous Patch Notes, we called out that the Patch will take a bit longer to go through certification on Nintendo, leaving the system temporarily out of version parity. We shared a warning about issues that may be incurred by playing on the Switch 2 if you’ve linked other platform accounts and wanted to explain that a little better.
What does “Out of Parity” mean?
This happens when one platform is on a version number different from other platforms. It’s often caused by taking longer for a Patch to be certified by the platform.
Can I still play on a platform that’s “Out of Parity”?
Yes! You should have nothing to be concerned about; you just won’t be able to play with players on other platforms during this time. The only exception is the following question.
What happens if I have Cross-Progression enabled and I play on an “Out of Parity” platform?

If you have linked your platform accounts to enable Cross-Progression across platforms, and one platform is out of parity, we recommend playing only on the platform that is up to date during this time. We don’t expect any permanent harm to your account or your character progression if you do otherwise, but you may encounter some weirdness in your Mission and Tasks progress during this time. This should return to normal once parity is restored.
What happens to cosmetics and other items I earn while I play on an “Out of Parity” platform?

Those will all be saved as normal and be available across platforms without issues. The only instance where something is saved to only one platform is when buying a Supporter Pack, due to platform limitations.

We’ve seen some questions about why the "Miner Miracle" Sticker is added to your Stickerbook once you purchase the Engineering Pack. This is because the Palette in this Supporter Pack has three different versions that are intended to be unlocked as you make progress in this Sticker. The more resources you mine, the more progress you would make toward unlocking the "Dirtier Work" Palette, and ultimately the "Dirtiest Work" Palette.

Given the confusion we’ve seen around how this works, we’ve decided to instead simply grant all three Palettes immediately to anyone who has purchased this Pack or buys it in the future. The "Miner Miracle" Sticker will remain, but no rewards will be tied to it anymore. We think this is a fun mechanic, but we missed the mark on having the proper UX to explain the sticker-based gameplay. This change will go into effect today.
We will go back to the drawing board to rethink the idea of progressive Palettes, and you may see this again in the future as part of a Community Challenge.

For new players who are just jumping into STARSEEKER, Community Challenges are just what they sound like. Astroneers aboard the ESS Starseeker must all work together toward contributing the Challenge’s requested items in order to unlock a new Region. In this case, that’s the Tangle!
When a new Region unlocks, the whole community gains access to new Missions, new craftable items, and new adventures! You’ll learn more about it as we approach its release.

For our first post-launch patch, we focused on addressing some of our most common crashes and connection issues, as well as a couple of places we saw performance dips in the game. This patch also includes a handful of gameplay updates, bug fixes, and even a few bits of polish!

Nintendo Delay: Patch 1.0.6 will be delayed for the Nintendo Switch 2, instead, this platform will be updated to Patch 1.0.5. We’ll share messaging on our social channels once the update has passed certification and is going live.

Cross-Progression Warning: If you play on the Switch 2 and have more than one Platform linked for cross-progression, then we recommend playing only on the platform with the latest version of the game available. Avoid playing on the Switch 2 only in this case, until the latest patch has released on Nintendo.
Cross-Play Warning: While the Switch 2 version is mismatched to other platforms, multiplayer won’t work across platforms to the Switch 2.

Steam Store Tags: Shortly after launch, we decided we should remove the “Single Player” tag from the game since it was misleading players on what we meant. While you’re able to queue alone for Expeditions and are never forced to join a Squad of other players, you do need to play online and other players will always be around you.
AG-18011 – The objective for JAM-BX's Mission 'Let's Get Clinical' no longer requests an item before its crafting Blueprint has been unlocked.

Developer Note: While most players were getting through this Mission by stumbling upon the required item in caches, the intended experience is that players are able to craft an item before it becomes required for Mission progress. Except for Ensign Muriel’s Missions. She’s just eccentric.
AG-17900 – To assist with readability, Crew Member Mission text now stays on screen longer.
AG-18086 – To assist with wayfinding, the type and size of waypoint icons have been adjusted in the Tutorial for the Depot and the Landing Zone.
Addressed our most common GPU start up crash.
Added a number of fixes for observed server crashes.
Fixed a common source of performance decline encountered during Expeditions.
Fixed a common source of performance decline on the ESS Starseeker, when rendering the player’s avatar on the station signs.
Fixed an issue that showed unreleased cosmetic items in the Customizer. Nothing to see here, move along.
AG-15001 – Made improvements to address an issue where players can appear invisible to their squadmates after landing on Tephra.

Developer Note: This bug has been harder for us to pin down, and we’ve issued a number of fixes for it over the course of Beta testing. We may need to continue deploying fixes until we fully resolve the problem.
AG-4153 – Fixed an issue where synced emotes were not properly showing across different clients.
AG-11707 – Added missing Crew Member idle animations.
AG-17894 – Fixed an issue that could allow players to move around while in a downed state after opening Planet View.
AG-18028 – Made improvements to address a UI memory leak. Additional fixes will come in future patches, but this should reduce the occurrence.
AG-17906 – Fixed an issue that could cause cinematics to stretch on ultrawide monitors. They are now properly locked to a 16:9 ratio. No more Widestroneers.
AG-18144 – Fixed an issue that was preventing all three Palettes included in the Engineering Pack from appearing in the in-game EXO Outlet preview.

Since there will be a delay for getting Patch 1.0.6 certified by Nintendo, today’s patch will bring the Switch 2 version of the game to version 1.0.5 instead, with the following changes. We’ll share messaging on our social channels once the update has passed certification and is going live.
AG-17880 – Moved the Backpack V3 reward out of the Wetlands Mission chain to later in the player progression.
AG-16156 – Fixed the ‘Fit Check’ Sticker notification so it no longer triggers with every completed Expedition.
AG-15094 – Fixed an issue affecting the progress bar on “Press and Hold” actions on the Nintendo Switch 2.
AG-17966 – Fixed an error that would not properly track ownership of the Engineering Pack cosmetics across different platforms.
